concept.name: Volume bar
concept.definition: A volume bar is an OHLCV bar built by aggregating trades until a fixed cumulative quantity (e.g., 10,000 shares or 100 BTC) has traded. Bars are thus sampled in units of traded volume rather than time or trade count.
concept.intuition: Each bar represents the same amount of actual participation — the market 'votes' with quantity, and a new bar is cast once the vote count reaches the threshold.
concept.mechanics: Accumulate traded quantities from the tick stream; when cumulative volume reaches the threshold V*, reduce the accumulated trades to OHLCV and reset. Volume bars sample more frequently when large traders are active and partially mitigate the trade-fragmentation distortion of tick bars, since splitting an order into more prints does not change total volume.
concept.failure_modes: A single block trade larger than the threshold straddles multiple bars or forces an oversized bar, depending on implementation, so bar-level volume is not exactly constant in practice. The threshold is arbitrary and not comparable across instruments of different liquidity.
concept.misconceptions: Volume bars do not have identical volumes in strict tick-level implementations unless trades are allowed to be split; many charting platforms approximate them from already-aggregated data, distorting the construction.
concept.example: With 50,000-share volume bars, if the tape prints 30k, 15k, and then 10k shares, the bar closes partway through the third print after exactly 50k shares have traded.

citations.source: López de Prado, Advances in Financial Machine Learning (Wiley, 2018)
